title.en: I'm going to walk; I'm meeting Jack
title.de: Pläne: I'm going to, I'm meeting
title.sl: Načrti: I'm going to, I'm meeting
title.it: I progetti: I'm going to, I'm meeting

goal.sl: Poveš, kaj nameravaš in kaj vidiš, da prihaja (I'm going to walk, It's going to rain), vprašaš po načrtih in poveš, kaj je dogovorjeno (I'm meeting Jack at ten).
goal.de: Du sagst, was du vorhast und was du kommen siehst (I'm going to walk, It's going to rain), fragst nach Plänen und sagst, was ausgemacht ist (I'm meeting Jack at ten).
goal.it: Dici che cosa vuoi fare e che cosa vedi arrivare (I'm going to walk, It's going to rain), chiedi dei progetti e dici che cosa è già fissato (I'm meeting Jack at ten).
goal.en: You can say what you plan to do and what you can see coming (I'm going to walk, It's going to rain), ask about plans, and say what is arranged (I'm meeting Jack at ten).

say.sl: Načrt, ki ga že imaš: **am**, **is** ali **are** + **going to** + osnovna oblika. **I'm going to walk to the tarn tomorrow.** (Jutri bom {m:šel|f:šla} peš do jezerca.) **Jack is going to clean the barn.** (Jack bo pospravil skedenj.) **We're going to paint the gate.** (Prebarvali bomo vrata.) Za **to** se glagol nikoli ne spremeni: **She's going to bake**, nikoli *She's going to bakes*.
say.de: Ein Plan, den du schon gemacht hast: **am**, **is** oder **are** + **going to** + Grundform. **I'm going to walk to the tarn tomorrow.** (Morgen gehe ich zum Bergsee.) **Jack is going to clean the barn.** (Jack räumt die Scheune auf.) **We're going to paint the gate.** (Wir streichen das Tor.) Nach **to** ändert sich das Verb nie: **She's going to bake**, nie *She's going to bakes*.
say.it: Un progetto già deciso: **am**, **is** o **are** + **going to** + la forma base. **I'm going to walk to the tarn tomorrow.** (Domani vado a piedi al laghetto.) **Jack is going to clean the barn.** (Jack pulirà il fienile.) **We're going to paint the gate.** (Dipingeremo il cancello.) Dopo **to** il verbo non cambia mai: **She's going to bake**, mai *She's going to bakes*.
say.en: A plan you have already made: **am**, **is** or **are** + **going to** + the base form. **I'm going to walk to the tarn tomorrow.** **Jack is going to clean the barn.** **We're going to paint the gate.** After **to** the verb never changes: **She's going to bake** (never *She's going to bakes*).

examples.en: I'm going to walk to the tarn tomorrow.
examples.it: Domani vado a piedi al laghetto.

say.sl: Za zanikanje gre **not** za be: **I'm not going to stay.** (Ne bom {m:ostal|f:ostala}.) **Sam isn't going to sell the van.** (Sam ne bo prodal kombija.) Pri vprašanju gre be naprej: **Are you going to walk?** (Boš {m:šel|f:šla} peš?) **What are you going to do?** (Kaj boš {m:naredil|f:naredila}?) Kratki odgovor je brez going to: **Yes, I am.** (Ja.) **No, she isn't.** (Ne.)
say.de: Zum Verneinen kommt **not** nach be: **I'm not going to stay.** (Ich bleibe nicht.) **Sam isn't going to sell the van.** (Sam verkauft den Lieferwagen nicht.) Bei der Frage kommt be nach vorn: **Are you going to walk?** (Gehst du zu Fuß?) **What are you going to do?** (Was machst du?) Die Kurzantwort ist ohne going to: **Yes, I am.** (Ja.) **No, she isn't.** (Nein.)
say.it: Per dire di no, **not** va dopo be: **I'm not going to stay.** (Non mi fermo.) **Sam isn't going to sell the van.** (Sam non venderà il furgone.) Per chiedere, be va all'inizio: **Are you going to walk?** (Vai a piedi?) **What are you going to do?** (Che cosa farai?) La risposta breve è senza going to: **Yes, I am.** (Sì.) **No, she isn't.** (No.)
say.en: For no, **not** goes after be: **I'm not going to stay.** **Sam isn't going to sell the van.** To ask, be goes first: **Are you going to walk?** **What are you going to do?** The short answer has no going to: **Yes, I am.** **No, she isn't.**

examples.en: I'm not going to stay at the inn.
Sam isn't going to sell the van.
What are you going to do on Sunday?
Are you going to walk? — Yes, I am.

rows: isn't, aren't, I'm not + going to

say.sl: **going to** pove tudi, kar vidiš, da prihaja, tu in zdaj: **Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.** (Poglej tiste oblake! Deževalo bo.) **Careful! That glass is going to fall.** (Pazi! Tisti kozarec bo padel.) **Meg's very tired. She's going to sleep.** (Meg je zelo utrujena. Zaspala bo.) Nihče tega ni načrtoval: vidiš.
say.de: **going to** sagt auch, was du kommen siehst, hier und jetzt: **Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.** (Schau dir die Wolken an! Gleich regnet es.) **Careful! That glass is going to fall.** (Vorsicht! Das Glas fällt gleich.) **Meg's very tired. She's going to sleep.** (Meg ist sehr müde. Sie schläft gleich ein.) Niemand hat das geplant: Du siehst es.
say.it: **going to** dice anche ciò che vedi arrivare, qui e ora: **Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.** (Guarda quelle nuvole! Sta per piovere.) **Careful! That glass is going to fall.** (Attento! Quel bicchiere sta per cadere.) **Meg's very tired. She's going to sleep.** (Meg è molto stanca. Sta per addormentarsi.) Nessuno l'ha deciso: lo vedi.
say.en: **going to** also says what you can see coming, here and now: **Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.** **Careful! That glass is going to fall.** **Meg's very tired. She's going to sleep.** Nobody planned it: you can see it.

say.sl: Kar je dogovorjeno, z uro in pogosto z drugimi: **am**, **is**, **are** + **-ing**. **I'm meeting Jack at ten.** (Ob desetih se dobim z Jackom.) **We're having dinner at the inn tonight.** (Nocoj večerjamo v gostilni.) **Mr Dixon is seeing the doctor on Friday.** (Gospod Dixon gre v petek k zdravniku.) Je že v koledarju. Povej, kdaj, sicer pomeni zdaj.
say.de: Was fix ausgemacht ist, mit Uhrzeit und oft mit anderen: **am**, **is**, **are** + **-ing**. **I'm meeting Jack at ten.** (Um zehn treffe ich Jack.) **We're having dinner at the inn tonight.** (Heute Abend essen wir im Gasthaus.) **Mr Dixon is seeing the doctor on Friday.** (Mr Dixon geht am Freitag zum Arzt.) Es steht schon im Kalender. Sag dazu, wann, sonst heißt es: jetzt.
say.it: Ciò che è già fissato, con un'ora e spesso con altri: **am**, **is**, **are** + **-ing**. **I'm meeting Jack at ten.** (Alle dieci vedo Jack.) **We're having dinner at the inn tonight.** (Stasera ceniamo alla locanda.) **Mr Dixon is seeing the doctor on Friday.** (Venerdì Mr Dixon va dal medico.) È già in agenda. Di' quando, se no vuol dire adesso.
say.en: What is arranged, with a time and often with someone else: **am**, **is**, **are** + **-ing**. **I'm meeting Jack at ten.** **We're having dinner at the inn tonight.** **Mr Dixon is seeing the doctor on Friday.** It is already in the diary. Say when, or it means now.

say.sl: Slovenščina za načrt pogosto reče sedanjik (*Jutri grem k babici*), angleščina nikoli: **I'm going to visit Granny tomorrow.** ali **I'm visiting Granny tomorrow.** (Jutri grem k babici.) Za to, kar je v koledarju, je prav oboje. Vreme, ki ga nihče ne dogovori, vzame **going to**: **It's going to snow.** (Snežilo bo.)
say.de: Deutsch sagt für einen Plan oft das Präsens (*Morgen besuche ich Oma*), Englisch nicht: **I'm going to visit Granny tomorrow.** oder **I'm visiting Granny tomorrow.** (Morgen besuche ich Oma.) Für das, was im Kalender steht, passt beides. Das Wetter, das niemand ausmacht, nimmt **going to**: **It's going to snow.** (Es wird schneien.)
say.it: L'italiano per un progetto dice spesso il presente (*Domani vado dalla nonna*), l'inglese no: **I'm going to visit Granny tomorrow.** o **I'm visiting Granny tomorrow.** (Domani vado dalla nonna.) Per ciò che è in agenda vanno bene tutti e due. Il tempo, che nessuno fissa, vuole **going to**: **It's going to snow.** (Nevicherà.)
say.en: Your language may say the present for a plan, but English doesn't: **I'm going to visit Granny tomorrow.** or **I'm visiting Granny tomorrow.** (never *I visit Granny tomorrow.*) For what is in the diary either is right. The weather, which nobody arranges, takes **going to**: **It's going to snow.**

examples.en: I'm going to visit Granny tomorrow.
I'm visiting Granny tomorrow.
It's going to snow tonight.

say.sl: V govoru **going to** pogosto zveni kot **gonna**: **I'm gonna be late.** (Zamudil{m:|f:a} bom.) V govoru je to prav, v pismo napiši **going to**. Z načrti gredo **tomorrow** (jutri), **tonight** (nocoj), **next week** (naslednji teden), **on Saturday** (v soboto), **soon** (kmalu): **We're going to sell the lambs next week.** (Naslednji teden bomo prodali jagnjeta.)
say.de: Beim Sprechen klingt **going to** oft wie **gonna**: **I'm gonna be late.** (Ich komme zu spät.) Gesprochen ist das richtig, im Brief schreibst du **going to**. Zu Plänen passen **tomorrow** (morgen), **tonight** (heute Abend), **next week** (nächste Woche), **on Saturday** (am Samstag), **soon** (bald): **We're going to sell the lambs next week.** (Nächste Woche verkaufen wir die Lämmer.)
say.it: Parlando **going to** suona spesso come **gonna**: **I'm gonna be late.** (Farò tardi.) A voce va bene, in una lettera scrivi **going to**. Con i progetti vanno **tomorrow** (domani), **tonight** (stasera), **next week** (la settimana prossima), **on Saturday** (sabato), **soon** (presto): **We're going to sell the lambs next week.** (La settimana prossima venderemo gli agnelli.)
say.en: In talk **going to** often sounds like **gonna**: **I'm gonna be late.** It's right when you speak; in a letter write **going to**. With plans go **tomorrow**, **tonight**, **next week**, **on Saturday**, **soon**: **We're going to sell the lambs next week.**

examples.en: I'm gonna be late.
We're going to sell the lambs next week.

examples.it: La settimana prossima venderemo gli agnelli.

translation.sl: V soboto je ples v gostilni Packhorse. Gospa Birkett bo skuhala juho za vse. — Kaj boš {m:počel|f:počela} ti, Jack? — Prinesel bom stole iz skednja. — Bo Sam pomagal? — Ne. Ob dveh se dobi s prijateljem v Keswicku. — Poglej nebo! Deževalo bo. — Potem bomo plesali notri.
translation.de: Am Samstag ist Tanz im Gasthaus Packhorse. Mrs Birkett macht Suppe für alle. — Was machst du, Jack? — Ich bringe die Stühle aus der Scheune. — Hilft Sam? — Nein. Er trifft um zwei einen Freund in Keswick. — Schau dir den Himmel an! Gleich regnet es. — Dann tanzen wir drinnen.
translation.it: Sabato c'è un ballo alla locanda Packhorse. Mrs Birkett farà la zuppa per tutti. — Tu che cosa fai, Jack? — Porto le sedie dal fienile. — Sam aiuta? — No. Alle due vede un amico a Keswick. — Guarda il cielo! Sta per piovere. — Allora balliamo dentro.
translation.en: On Saturday there's a dance at the Packhorse Inn. Mrs Birkett is going to make soup for everyone. — What are you going to do, Jack? — I'm going to bring the chairs from the barn. — Is Sam going to help? — No, he isn't. He's meeting a friend in Keswick at two. — Look at the sky! It's going to rain. — Then we are going to dance inside.

translation.sl: — Kaj boš počel v nedeljo, Arthur? — Pogledal bom svoje čebele. — Bo babica Maggie pekla? — Ja. In ob štirih pijemo čaj s starim Wilfom. Vse je dogovorjeno. — Poglej tiste oblake! Snežilo bo.
translation.de: — Was machst du am Sonntag, Arthur? — Ich schaue nach meinen Bienen. — Bäckt Oma Maggie? — Ja. Und um vier trinken wir Tee mit dem alten Wilf. Es ist alles ausgemacht. — Schau dir die Wolken an! Es wird schneien.
translation.it: — Che cosa fai domenica, Arthur? — Vado a vedere le mie api. — Nonna Maggie prepara i dolci? — Sì. E alle quattro prendiamo il tè con il vecchio Wilf. È tutto fissato. — Guarda quelle nuvole! Sta per nevicare.
translation.en: — What are you going to do on Sunday, Arthur? — I'm going to look at my bees. — Is Granny Maggie going to bake? — Yes, she is. And at four we're having tea with Old Wilf. It's all arranged. — Look at those clouds! It is going to snow.
